business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Medical Record (EMR) Clinical Workflow Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (Grand Duchy of Luxembourg; unitary national jurisdiction, no sub-state corporate carve-outs)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Income Tax Treaty (1996, as amended by the 2009 Protocol)
Luxembourg–Germany Double Tax Agreement (2012, as amended by the 2014 Protocol)
Luxembourg–Hong Kong Double Tax Agreement (2007, as amended by the 2014 Protocol)
Luxembourg–United Kingdom Double Tax Agreement (1967, as amended in 2008, surviving in revised post-Brexit form)
OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI), effective in Luxembourg from 1 August 2019
Luxembourg bilateral investment treaties concluded with non-EU jurisdictions and Benelux Union investment-protection arrangements
EU–Canada CETA and EU–Japan EPA applicable through Luxembourg as an EU member state

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (transposing EU AMLD 4, AMLD 5 and AMLD 6); CSSF Regulation N° 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs – RBE), as amended; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 7 February 2019 on the RBE; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended, Articles 90-1 et seq. governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Constitution deed (contrat de société) of the SCSp comprising the full partnership agreement, executed before a Luxembourg notary as the recommended route; alternatively a private writing with legalized signatures, requiring LBR acceptance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: National notarial deed; no apostille for domestic use; non-resident signatories execute through a notarized power of attorney carrying a Hague Apostille or consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Corporate authorization resolution, certificate of good standing and registry extract of the general partner where the GP is a legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry in the GP's country of origin; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) where the GP is Luxembourg-based
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille under the Hague Convention of 5 October 1961 for foreign-issued extracts; LBR e-certificate for Luxembourg issuers

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney (procuration) for the incorporation signatory and for any UBO declarant acting on behalf of non-resident limited partners
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction of the principal
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing jurisdiction is party to the Hague Convention; otherwise consular legalization at the Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO declaration (déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) identifying every natural person holding or controlling directly or indirectly more than 25% of the SCSp, or the statutory fallback declaration where exhaustive search identifies no natural person
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary and LBR RBE electronic filing module
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Executed before the incorporation notary and filed with the RBE; no apostille required; limited-partner data is masked to public-level access restrictions

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Judicial extracts (bulletin judiciaire No. 3) for each natural-person manager and general partner, accompanied by a completed PEP/sanctions screening output dossier
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Parquet Général du Luxembourg for the judicial extract; World-Check, LexisNexis or Dow Jones via a Luxembourg fiduciaire for the screening dossier
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: National extract authenticated by the issuing prosecutor's office; screening output is an internal compliance record and requires no legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Optional prior ministerial clearance certificate if the EMR brand name incorporates a reserved health-sector token such as 'medical', 'clinic' or 'hospice'
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Health and/or Ministry of the Economy of Luxembourg
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: National administrative act; no legalization required; to be deposited with the LBR file only if the sensitive name token is ultimately adopted

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under the Law of 12 November 2004 and CSSF Regulation 12-02 must be completed before inception: (i) identify and verify every general partner and every natural-person beneficial owner using official government-issued identification; (ii) screen all managers, the GP, all partners and the UBOs against UN sanctions, EU autonomous asset-freezing regulations (including Regulation (EU) No 269/2014), OFAC SDN, UK HMT and Luxembourg national asset-freezing lists; (iii) apply enhanced due diligence to all politically exposed persons (PEPs), their family members and close associates irrespective of nationality; (iv) apply the 25% look-through threshold with indirect-control analysis through nominee chains, trusts, foundations and intermediate legal entities, requiring full disclosure of any nominee arrangement; (v) retain all CDD records for at least five years following termination of the business relationship; and (vi) document all screening results in a dated, immutable file available for CSSF inspection. In line with the CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022 (Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20), Luxembourg has suspended general public access to the RBE; access is currently restricted to competent authorities and statutory obliged entities conducting AML/CFT due diligence.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), operated by LBR under the law of 19 June 2009 and accessible via the official portal at lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be expressed in Latin script; the distinctive element may be drafted in French, German, Luxembourgish or English; where a non-Latin-script brand is desired, a faithful Latin-script transliteration is mandatory for registration. The exact suffix 'SCSp' or the full legal form 'société en commandite spéciale' must follow the distinctive name element in all public documents. The name must not be misleading, contrary to public policy, or so similar to an existing RCS-registered name as to create a risk of confusion.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Luxembourg / Luxemburg used as a dominant name element without ministerial authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection of the proposed name by the LBR, the applicant may first file a written rectification request with LBR within 15 calendar days of the rejection notice, submitting comparative evidence of distinction from prior-registered names and, if applicable, the ministerial clearance for a sensitive token. If rejection is confirmed or if the applicant proceeds on procedural grounds, a judicial appeal lies to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) within one month of the final administrative decision; representation by a Luxembourg avocat à la Cour is mandatory. There is no separate statutory appeal fee beyond court disbursements of approximately EUR 400-600 and counsel fees on the market benchmark. The 30-day provisional name protection window lapses automatically if the notarial deed and RBE filings are not perfected within the window; an extension is available only where ministerial clearance proceedings are pending, in which case the applicant must re-secure the name immediately upon clearance.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Restricted permissibility. An SCSp must maintain a registered office in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg and retain the capacity to receive official correspondence. A serviced registered-office arrangement (domiciliation) through an authorized Luxembourg service provider (law firm, notary, auditor or approved fiduciaire) is acceptable for incorporation and filing purposes. However, for an ISIC 6201/NAICS 511210 cloud-based EMR SaaS business, a purely virtual or mail-forwarding address will undermine future tax-residency planning and administrative substance; the RCS and the Luxembourg direct tax authorities expect genuine physical correspondence capacity, local record retention and decision-making infrastructure. Virtual office is rated: permissible for registration only, disfavored for substance purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: Low-to-moderate. Estimated unannounced on-site inspection probability of 5-15% during the first 24 months for a standard IT-SaaS SCSp with clean UBO disclosure and ordinary name selection. The probability escalates to above 40% if a suspicious transaction report, OFAC/UN screening hit, PEP concentration, tax audit referral or incomplete RBE declaration triggers administrative scrutiny. The LBR may also verify the registered office under the amended Law of 10 August 1915; such verification is normally documentary, moving to an on-site visit only where red flags are present.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: LBR name availability search and provisional name-clearance report with 30-day reservation protection
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market tariff for online search preparation by an incorporated service provider; statutory query is zero-cost, professional report generates the fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Statutory RCS incorporation filing, deed deposit and registration in the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fee schedule for partnership/SCSp filings, approximately EUR 118-128, applied per the LBR published tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of constitution (SCSp partnership agreement, drafting, review, authentication and engrossment)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Notarial tariff based on declared contributions with statutory minimum; market benchmark EUR 2,300-2,900 given the zero-minimum-capital SCSp regime

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization bundle for foreign-issued general partner documents and powers of attorney (estimated three documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Luxembourg, Luxembourg embassy/consulate in source jurisdiction, and issuing Hague authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille tariff of approximately EUR 20-25 per document plus consular service fees of USD 100-150 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified sworn translation of corporate documents into French by a Luxembourg expert judiciaire
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator admitted before the Luxembourg Court of Appeal
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark rate of EUR 0.20-0.25 per word for an estimated 3,200-word bundle

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration and RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) electronic registration filing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory filing charge; the fee is absorbed in the notary's and counsel's professional fees

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO piercing analysis, PEP screening, OFAC/UN/EU/UK/Luxembourg sanctions screening dossier for all natural persons and the general partner
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance data vendor (LexisNexis/World-Check/Dow Jones) engaged through a Luxembourg fiduciaire
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Pro-rata annual list-access license of USD 900-1,100 plus investigative analyst time of two hours at prevailing market rates

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Annual registered-office domiciliation agreement with an approved Luxembourg service provider, including mail handling and governance assistance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg fiduciaire or law firm authorized to provide domiciliation services
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market annual domiciliation benchmark EUR 1,300-1,800; contract term commences at pre-incorporation booking

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal counsel pre-incorporation due diligence, SCSp partnership-agreement review, tax-transparency assessment, UBO-chain structure verification and filing protocol
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Avocat à la Cour (law firm)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed-fee engagement benchmark EUR 3,500-4,200, representing approximately eight to ten partner and associate hours

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Optional prior ministerial clearance for a health-sensitive name token (where the EMR brand incorporates 'clinic', 'medical' or a direct equivalent)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Health and/or Ministry of the Economy of Luxembourg
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Administrative fee per the applicable ministerial tariff; payable only if the sensitive token is included in the final name

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), in particular Articles 566-1 to 566-9 governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp), together with the Law of 31 May 2016 relating to partnerships, the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), and the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 29 January 2019 on the duties of the Luxembourg Business Registers.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), 6, rue Jean Engling, L-1466 Luxembourg; e-filing portal: https://www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Contrat de société / Statuts (SCSp Partnership Agreement), executed under private signature or by notarial deed, together with the Déclaration légale du gérant (Manager's Legal Declaration) and supporting annexes, e-filed with the RCS via LBR.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Luxembourg SCSp; the capital is freely fixed in the partnership agreement and may be subscribed in cash, in kind, or in industry. Cash contributions are typically credited to a Luxembourg bank account opened in the SCSp's name and evidenced by a banker's certificate of deposit; no legal escrow account is mandatory, but the certificate of deposit forms part of the RCS filing dossier.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: UNANIMOUS WRITTEN RESOLUTION OF THE SOLE GENERAL PARTNER of [Entity Name], dated [Date], adopted pursuant to the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended. 1. Subscriptions: The general partner accepts subscription commitments of EUR [Amount] for one Class A limited partnership interest held by the sole limited partner. 2. Registered Office: The registered office of the SCSp is fixed at 12, Rue de Vianden, L-2100 Luxembourg. 3. Officers: The general partner appoints [Name] as day-to-day manager (gérant) with joint signatory authority, and [Name] as AML Compliance Officer, each until revoked. 4. Filing: The gérant is authorized to execute and file all RCS registration documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Partners acting under private signature or, optionally, a Notary Public registered in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement and the special limited partnership terms, including the registered office, corporate purpose limited to software development and EMR/medical SaaS activities, classes of interests, capital commitments, general partner rights, transfer restrictions, and governance quorum rules. Execute the instrument either under private signature or, where immovable property is contributed, by notarial deed; a cash-only SaaS SCSp may validly use a private deed.
required_dossiers: Nomination and written consent of the sole general partner
Identification documents and proof of residential address of all partners
Capital contribution schedule and allocation of Class A limited partnership interests
Executed draft partnership agreement or notarial deed, if used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the deed at filing stage, execute a corrective rider (avenant) to the partnership agreement signed by all partners re-stating the disputed clause; re-submission of the correcting private deed is sufficient.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Manager (Gérant) Criminal Record and Capacity Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of Justice – Criminal Records Service (Bulletin n°2 / Casier judiciaire) via https://criminalrecords.public.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a bulletin n°2 (extract of the criminal record) for each proposed day-to-day manager (gérant), proving absence of disqualifying convictions for bankruptcy, business interdiction, or commercial crimes. For non-resident managers, obtain the equivalent extract from the competent authorities of the EEA or third country of residence. The extract must be dated no more than three months before the RCS filing.
required_dossiers: Request form for criminal record bulletin n°2
Identity document of the manager
Proof of current municipal registration (commune) for Luxembourg residents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the criminal record extract is delayed, file a sworn statement with the RCS declaring the absence of disqualifying convictions and submit the official extract immediately upon issuance; the RCS customarily accepts this interim attestation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the SCSp Bank Account and Capital Contribution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Credit institution in Luxembourg (e.g., BIL, BGL BNP Paribas, Spuerkeess, ING Luxembourg) or an authorized PSD2/electronic-money institution subject to the Law of 18 April 2020 on the fight against money laundering
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Present the executed partnership agreement, the RCS dossier number, and the resolutions of the general partner to the compliance officer of the credit institution. Complete beneficial-owner KYC and manager KYC procedures. Fund the subscription amount (no minimum statutory threshold) by wire transfer; instruct the bank to issue a certificate of deposit (attestation de dépôt de fonds) naming the SCSp, which will be exhibited to the RCS upon registration.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the executed partnership agreement
Updated identification and residence evidence for each beneficial owner
Original passport and current address proof for the gérant
Business description and projected SaaS billing model (AML low-risk form)
Bank certificate of the subscription amount received on the account
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the compliance request is refused, cooperate with the bank's AML desk to provide the customer wire map of the SaaS clients (Stripe Billing / bank transfer rails) and, if still refused, open the account with another licensed institution; the certificate of deposit must always be issued in the name of the SCSp.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration via Luxembourg Business Registers e-Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés e-filing portal at https://www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the LBR e-filing interface, create the company file, upload the executed partnership agreement, the manager's sworn declaration of office acceptance and signature mandate, the registered-office acceptance letter of the Luxembourg address provider, and the bank's certificate of deposit. Pay the registration fee online by bank card. The RCS examiner verifies the deed, the capital evidence, and the managers' consents; on approval, the registry number (numéro RCS) is assigned and the legal entity comes into existence.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement (contrat de société) in PDF
Sworn declaration of office acceptance (déclaration légale) of the gérant
Registered-office acceptance letter from the Luxembourg address provider or landlord
Bank certificate of deposit of the capital contribution
Criminal record bulletin n°2 of the manager
Identity and address documentation of the general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises a query (lettre de suite), respond within 15 calendar days with corrected filings or supplemental declarations; late responses attract a surcharge of EUR 150 per month. Engage local legal counsel to draft the remedial statement and re-file electronically.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RESA Publication and Beneficial Owner (RBE) Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – automatic RESA publication; Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) online portal at https://www.rbe.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the RCS registration order, the registrar automatically publishes the legal excerpt of the constitution in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA). Concurrently, file the RBE declaration identifying every individual ultimately owning or controlling more than 25% of the SCSp interests or otherwise exercising control. The RBE declaration must be lodged within 30 days of the registration of the SCSp.
required_dossiers: RCS registration order confirming the SCSp deposit
RBE form with the breakdown of beneficial ownership percentages
Consent of each beneficial owner and supporting passport copies
Identity and control documents of each beneficial owner
Any prior tax identification number, if already obtained
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late RBE filing is punishable by fines up to EUR 1,250 and criminal penalties up to 6 months' imprisonment; file a corrective declaration immediately through the RBE portal and, if fined, submit an executive remonstrance with the RBE registrar together with proof of the timely initial deposit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Ministry of the Economy – Direction Générale des Classes Moyennes / Entreprises platform at https://guichet.public.lu (myguichet.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Because software development is a commercial activity, the SCSp's general partner must hold a valid 'autorisation d'établissement' or obtain an exemption for the SCSp trade. File the application through myguichet.lu using the SCSp RCS number, the gérant's identity document, the criminal record bulletin, and proof of professional capacity (diploma or documented three-year professional experience). The authorization is personal and issued for the specific activity code corresponding to ISIC 62.01 / Computer programming, SaaS and related services.
required_dossiers: Completed myguichet.lu business-establishment application form
Copy of the RCS registration certificate of the SCSp
Identity document and criminal record bulletin of the gérant
Professional capacity evidence (diploma or prior employment certificates)
Simple financial statement of solvency
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Ministry issues a request for additional documentation, respond within one month through the myguichet.lu statement-of-deficiencies module; thereafter, an administrative appeal (recours) to the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg is available within three months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Data Protection and Health-Data Posture Registration (CNPD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commission Nationale pour la Protection des Données (CNPD) via the online declaration service at https://cnpd.public.lu; where the EMR service qualifies as a health information-system service, coordination with the Ministry of Health / eHealth Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a GDPR Article 30 Record of Processing Activities; where the SCSp acts as processor for medical clinics, execute an Article 28 Data Processing Agreement; submit the CNPD processing notification form; and, if the EMR software is classified as a medical device under EU MDR 2017/745, appoint a European Authorised Representative and register the device with the competent health authority before market placement.
required_dossiers: GDPR Article 30 Record of Processing Activities
CNPD notification form (déclaration de traitement)
Data Processing Agreement template between the SCSp and clinical customers
European Authorised Representative agreement, where applicable
Technical security documentation demonstrating encryption, access control, and audit logging
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CNPD returns the declaration, correct the filing within 30 days; in case of an audit, present the security measures and the Record of Processing Activities to demonstrate proportionality and submit the corrected declaration before any enforcement measure.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie – Direction de la Promotion de l'Économie (business establishment authorization); Ministère de la Santé – Direction de la Santé (eHealth/medical software registration, where the EMR SaaS is characterized as a medical device under EU MDR 2017/745)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Authorization) under the Law of 2 September 2011 on access to the professions of artisan, shopkeeper, manufacturer and certain liberal professions, as amended; supplemented, where applicable, by EU Medical Device Regulation 2017/745 registration and the Luxembourg health-data processing permit for the EMR platform.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no EIA required. Office-based software development (NACE 62.01 / ISIC 6201) is not listed in the Annex of the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment; the SCSp does not operate an industrial installation subject to the commodo/incommodo environmental permit.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater, stack emissions, or VOC sources are generated. Office operations remain below Luxembourg municipal thresholds for wastewater discharge (generally ≤30 m³/day), and all waste streams, including electronic waste, are sorted via accredited collectors (Oekozenter Lëtzebuerg) under the national waste plan and EU WEEE/RoHS Directives. Where the SCSp co-locates servers, cooling installations must respect EU Regulation No 517/2014 on fluorinated greenhouse gases, and any emergency generator below the 20 MW thermal threshold is not subject to the Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety: the office premises must be certified for fire alarm, extinguishers, emergency lighting, and evacuation routes under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 22 July 2014 and municipal fire-prevention rules. Structural load: the building-permit and certificate-of-conformity (certificat de conformité) files must be maintained at the registered office. Occupational health: the SCSp must register with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) as an employer, file the annual declaration of posts, and comply with the Law of 17 April 2019 on workplace conditions, including workstation ergonomics, electrical safety, and lighting thresholds; employees using screens for more than two continuous hours require the documented arrangements for protective eye examinations under national occupational-health rules.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg Inland Revenue (Administration des contributions directes – ACD) for direct taxes; Registration Duties, Estates and VAT Authority (Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA – AEDT) for indirect taxes; integrated corporate and tax registration portal: guichet.lu and Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing or registering as a Luxembourg SCSp must first file the partnership deed with the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) and obtain a RCS registration number. The RCS number serves as the national business registration identifier. Subsequently, the SCSp must apply for a Luxembourg VAT identification number from the AEDT, using Form 642 (application for VAT registration), accompanied by the RCS extract, partnership deed, proof of place of effective management or fixed establishment in Luxembourg, and identification of all partners, including foreign partners. Foreign partnerships without a Luxembourg fixed establishment for VAT purposes may require a domestic VAT representative; a non-resident partner with taxable Luxembourg income may further need to register with the ACD for direct tax compliance and obtain a Luxembourg tax number (numéro d'identification collective / n° matricule). The applicant must submit the application via the AES (Registre électronique des agents) / MyGuichet.lu secure portal, and the AEDT typically issues the VAT number within 3 to 10 business days after receipt of complete documentation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Luxembourg SCSp is fiscally transparent by default and is not subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax or municipal business tax; income and gains are taxed directly in the hands of partners. Luxembourg law does not provide an elective 'check-the-box' regime equivalent to the U.S. check-the-box system. However, certain elections can affect classification: (i) the SCSp may elect to be treated as an 'assujetti unique' for VAT purposes by forming a VAT grouping, which consolidates multiple related entities into one taxable person; (ii) in cross-border hybrid arrangements, the SCSp's transparency can be confirmed or modified by the ACD through a tax ruling (advance tax decision) under the Luxembourg Circular L.I.R. n° 14/4, provided the foreign tax treatment of the SCSp is demonstrated, allowing application of hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD 2; (iii) where the SCSp has a commercial activity and is not a pure asset-holding vehicle, the partners can effectively select the method of profit allocation under the partnership agreement, subject to arm's length and substance requirements. No election exists to convert the SCSp into a fully taxable corporation without a change of legal form, but it may be transformed into a S.à r.l. or S.A. with tax-neutral reorganisation rules in limited circumstances.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée – TVA), Luxembourg national VAT system in conformity with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Under Luxembourg law, a taxable person may qualify for the small business exemption where annual taxable turnover (excluding VAT) does not exceed EUR 30,000. This threshold applies to supplies of goods and services made within Luxembourg by an entity established in Luxembourg, subject to exclusion for intra-Community acquisitions and for certain cross-border services that trigger mandatory registration, including electronically supplied services (SaaS/cloud EMR) and reverse-charge transactions where the customer is a taxable person established elsewhere in the EU. For an SCSp engaged in medical-clinic EMR SaaS with cross-border clients, the EUR 30,000 threshold is generally not effective to avoid registration where any B2B client is VAT-registered in another EU Member State; VAT registration in Luxembourg and/or identification through OSS (Union scheme) becomes mandatory regardless of domestic turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg has no mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control, or digital stamping mandate applicable to private B2B e-invoicing as of the current tax reporting period. E-invoicing is permitted under the general invoicing rules; invoices must comply with VAT invoicing requirements (Article 59 of the Luxembourg VAT law) and may be issued in electronic format subject to authenticity of origin, integrity of content, and readability. Public sector e-invoicing (B2G) is mandatory and operates through the PEPPOL BIS 3.0 network. VAT returns and EU sales listings (recapitulative statements) must be filed electronically via the eCDF / MyGuichet.lu portal; periodic standard VAT returns follow the calendar quarter generally, with monthly filing required for taxpayers exceeding certain thresholds; annual returns are mandatory. Cross-border digitally supplied services (medical software SaaS) must be reported through the OSS non-Union/Union scheme where applicable, and reverse-charge mechanisms on B2B supplies are subject to the normal EU place-of-supply rules. The AEDT may require historic invoice logs and structured e-invoice extraction during audits, and taxpayers must maintain sufficient electronic records for reconstruction of transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: exports dispatched or transported outside the European Union qualify for 0% VAT where the exporter proves that the goods left EU territory within the legal timeframe (generally 90 days where transport is evidenced by transport documents) and that the recipient is a non-EU person. For services: SaaS/EMR medical-clinic software qualifies for zero-rating or no-Place-of-Supply taxation in Luxembourg where supplied to a non-EU customer (B2B or B2C effective use outside Luxembourg) and where the service is considered 'export' under Article 58 or Article 59 of the Luxembourg VAT law; B2B supplies to EU customers are taxable in the customer's country via reverse charge (article 44 EU VAT Directive), while B2C supplies of electronic services to non-EU consumers are zero-rated or outside the scope under the OSS Non-Union procedure. Zero-rating also applies to exports of ancillary goods (e.g., hardware/tablets pre-loaded with EMR software) only when a valid customs export declaration is made. Quantitative or qualitative conditions include (i) the exporter holds a valid status as a taxable person, (ii) outgoing cross-border movement of goods is substantiated with transport evidence, and (iii) for services, the effective use and enjoyment test or customer-established place requirement is met.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EMCS / NES Lodged and Customs-approved Single Administrative Document or electronic declaration via Luxembourg Single Window)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill / CMR transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank transfer confirmation proving payment received from non-resident customer
Commercial invoice with explicit zero-rate VAT clause and Incoterms
Proof of delivery — signed POD, customs seal record, or arrival stamp in destination non-EU country
Customer's VAT registration certificate or non-resident supplier declaration evidencing the customer's establishment outside Luxembourg
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT and Luxembourg Customs may conduct ex-post audits of zero-rating claims, requiring strict documentary correlation between export declarations, transport documents, payment flows, and accounting records. Misstated or fraudulent zero-rated export claims trigger reassessment of unpaid VAT at the standard 17% rate, plus default interest calculated at the statutory rate (currently 5% per annum, adjusted from time to time) running from the date the VAT fell due. Deliberate fraud or knowingly false declarations incur a tax penalty of between 10% and 20% of the tax evaded, while criminal prosecution under Articles 309 and 310 of the Luxembourg Criminal Code can result in fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years for the person responsible. Additionally, the taxable person may lose the right to zero-rating for future transactions, be removed from the OSS scheme, be jointly and severally liable for unpaid VAT, and, in the case of abusive or artificial arrangements, face retrospective clawback under the anti-abuse rules and GAAR (Article 6 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law) with recharacterisation of the transaction as a domestic taxable supply.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), operating within the European System of Central Banks and under the prudential supervision framework jointly co-ordinated by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the European Central Bank (ECB) for euro area monetary policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a fully integrated member of the euro area; the euro is freely convertible for both current and capital account transactions in line with Articles 63-65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and the OECD Code of Liberalisation of Capital Movements. Capital account operations, including equity subscription to an SCSp, cross-border loans, and repatriation of profits, are unrestricted for EU/EEA residents and generally permitted for non-residents. No prior foreign exchange authorisation, surrender or approval requirement applies. Profit remittance is subject only to standard corporate/income tax confirmation of beneficial ownership and, for partnerships, the tax transparency treatment of the SCSp means no withholding tax at entity level. Any distribution to non-resident partners may trigger only domestic rules if the partner is a corporate entity in a non-treaty jurisdiction; no exchange control barrier exists. The EMR SaaS business, being a cloud-based software exporter, enjoys full current account convertibility for subscription billing in USD, EUR, and other major currencies.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory conversion ratios under Luxembourg law. Exporters of software services, including licence fees, maintenance, and cloud subscription revenue, may retain receipts in foreign currency in domestic or cross-border bank accounts. The BCL only collects statistics for balance-of-payments reporting; enterprises are required to report cross-border payments of more than EUR 12,500 per individual transaction to the BCL for statistical purposes via the BCL's report system. No specific conversion to euros is required.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: High for ancillary payments collection, but constrained for core treasury cash management. Luxembourg recognises Payment Institutions (PI) and Electronic Money Institutions (EMI) authorised under CSSF in line with the revised Payment Services Directive (PSD2). An offshore EMI without a Luxembourg or EU passport may not provide regulated payment services in Luxembourg. A cross-border EMI licensed in another EEA state may, under the freedom of establishment and passporting regime, open a single-currency or multi-currency account for the SCSp and process card and bank transfer payments. However, the SCSp will still require a tier-1 Luxembourg or EU credit institution for all material liquidity, debt, escrow, and guaranteed clearing transactions. The legal constraint is that an EMI cannot provide overdraft, credit, or any interest-bearing deposit product; all client funds must be safeguarded via a segregated account at a credit institution. For the EMR SaaS model, an EMI such as a Passported Fintech (e.g., Adyen, Airwallex, or similar) can be viable only as an additional collection rail for high-voltage, low-ticket subscription fees, while primary settlement must remain in a fully licensed bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg anti-money laundering (AML) law (Law of 12 November 2004, as amended, and CSSF Regulation 12-02) imposes a risk-based customer due diligence process. A physical presence of directors is not an absolute statutory mandate, but for an SCSp with pass-through classification, non-resident managers, and a non-resident ultimate beneficial owner (UBO), most Luxembourg tier-1 banks will require at least one in-person interview at the bank's office in Luxembourg, or a video conference interview followed by notarised/certified identity verification, before final account approval. The CSSF strongly expects obliged entities to identify and verify UBOs with reliable, independent source documentation. Where no director is physically available, a remote onboarding dossier supported by apostilled corporate documents, bank reference letters, and certified copies from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS) may satisfy KYC, but the decision remains within the bank's compliance risk appetite. For the EMR SaaS commercial model (a low-risk activity under AML risk classification), the mandate is reduced; physical presence is usually waived if remote verification is augmented by video interview and biometric identity proof of each director and UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO identification for a partnership with no minimum capital and fully pass-through character; the RCS does not require public filing of the UBO register for SCSp.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarised extract of the partnership agreement (contrat de société), an internal UBO register listing each natural person owning or controlling more than 25% of capital or voting rights, a sworn statement of beneficial ownership signed by all general partners, and a legal opinion from a Luxembourg avocat confirming the SCSp's transparency status. Include organisational charts and source-of-funds documentation for each UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors or managers domiciled in higher-risk or non-EU jurisdictions, triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply a professional background check, passport copies, proof of residential address not older than three months, an official certificate of good conduct from the country of residence, a banker's reference letter from their personal home bank, and a detailed CV or track record of similar healthcare technology operations. Where applicable, provide an international police clearance certificate, and evidence of any licensing overseas (e.g., HIPAA compliance attestation in the United States).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for the initial capital subscription into the SCSp: banks may question the economic substance of a zero-minimum-capital partnership with early capital injections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a comprehensive treasury projection for the EMR SaaS business, audited or reviewed financial statements of investors, tax returns of the funding entities, transactional bank statements covering the previous 12 months, and an executed subscription/ capital contribution agreement. Include a legal note rebutting any migration or tax-evasion inference, and where the capital derives from a holding company in another EU state, provide corporate registry extracts and proof of tax residence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: The medical-clinic EMR SaaS scope triggers concern about healthcare data privacy, possible 'safe-harbour' obligations, and potential future high-risk data flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Present a valid ISO 27001/ISO 27701 certification, a GDPR compliance framework with Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA), HIPAA Business Associate Agreement templates, BCL/CSSF data processing documentation, and a detailed product security white paper. Add a statement from the legal counsel confirming that the entity does not hold patient data directly and only serves medical clinics as a software provider with sub-processor arrangements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of an SCSp as a pass-through entity may trigger 'complex corporate structure' classification, requiring substantive documentation on the commercial rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a business plan showing the cross-border expansion of the EMR software into European and US markets, delineating why the SCSp vehicle was selected (flexibility, limited liability, contractual transparency), and include a formal written explanation of all current and anticipated fund flows. Add a Luxembourg tax opinion confirming that the entity is not a shell and will engage in genuine economic activity through employees, contracts, and funded development.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound capital injection into the SCSp from non-resident investors must be executed by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 (for high-value transactions) using the beneficiary account at a Luxembourg bank. The payment instruction must clearly state the beneficiary as 'LU_SCSP, Société en Commandite Spéciale' and include the purpose of payment code. For EU statistical reporting, use the BCL Balance of Payments classification code for equity capital injection (e.g., under direct investment, category 'Equity capital'). Recommended SWIFT purpose code is 'CAPT' (Capital Contribution) or a bilateral reference such as 'SCSp capital subscription'. The routing must be directly to the EUR IBAN of the operational account; if injected in USD, the receiving bank will convert at corporate rates or utilise a nostro Vostro arrangement. Mandatory verification for AML purposes includes a copy of the executed capital call notice, the partner's capital account ledger entry, and confirmation of the source of funds. The bank may require a certified copy of the subscribed capital entry in the internal accounts of the SCSp; no deposit of minimum capital is required, but the funds must be identifiable and traceable. Inbound payments from a non-EU jurisdiction of more than EUR 10,000 trigger direct control by the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) Luxembourg through the bank's automated monitoring system; no pre-clearance is required except for sanctions screening against target lists.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements and operating costs (software vendor payments, cloud hosting fees, medical-clinic partner commissions, and legal/consulting invoices) should be routed primarily through SWIFT MT103 individual customer credit transfers, ensuring correct KYC on beneficiaries and a precise remittance information field matching the underlying invoice. For high-volume recurring payments to EU suppliers, the SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) scheme offers cost-efficient EUR-denominated clearing; for USD disbursements, the bank's correspondent network and SWIFT MT103 are the standard rails. Where the SCSp enters into commercial contracts with major healthcare distributors, a Documentary Letter of Credit (Commercial LC) issued by a Luxembourg bank may be used; this is permissible provided the underlying transaction is genuine and the LC text reflects the specific SaaS deliverables. For subscription revenue collections from non-EU clients, the primary inbound rails should include Stripe Billing (with payout to the Luxembourg bank account) and direct SWIFT inbound via a multi-currency IBAN. All outbound cross-border payments must include the correct BCL statistical purpose code (e.g., 'Payment for IT services') and should be named in the accounting records to satisfy the annual statutory audit obligation under Luxembourg law. There is no currency-blocking mechanism, but the bank will require evidence of the commercial rationale for any unusually large outbound transfer from a newly funded SCSp, typically the purchase order, contract, or pro forma invoice, plus a confirmation from directors that the payment is not a hidden distribution.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards (Outright Forward Contracts) in EUR/USD and EUR/CHF, with a maximum tenor of 12 months, used to hedge subscription revenues and vendor costs; no premium required and fully available within the current global bank ability.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in exotic currencies (e.g., INR, PHP, BRL) where local deliverability is restricted, using EUR or USD as reference; permitted if held with a Luxembourg or EEA investment firm and only for cash-settled hedging of commercial receivables.

Currency Swaps (FX Cross-Currency Swaps) between EUR and USD or EUR/GBP for managing medium-term working capital mismatches; allowed only for risk management and requiring an ISDA Master Agreement with a bank counterparty.

FX Options (Call and Put) on the EUR/USD pair, either vanilla or collar structures, purchased or sold solely to hedge budgeted foreign-currency exposures; any structured option must comply with MiFID II product governance and be transacted through an authorised investment firm.

Basis swaps and short-term EUR/USD money market swaps, used exclusively for interest rate and liquidity management on the SCSp cash pool, with the condition that the bank reserves the right to refuse speculative positions.

Dynamic Currency Overlay (FX Sweep) services in the operational account, automating conversion of foreign currency receivables into EUR above a threshold; this is classified as a treasury service rather than a derivative and requires a signed international treasury management agreement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS update declaration (declaration annuelle) confirming the registered particulars of the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Registre de Commerce et des Societes (RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between 1 January and 31 May for existing registrations; for an SCSp registered during the year, within one month of the date of its RCS registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: After a formal electronic reminder, an administrative fine of up to EUR 500 (approx. USD 550) may be imposed per missing declaration under Article 35 of the RCS Law; persistent default enables the Public Prosecutor to seek a court order striking the SCSp off the RCS, with publication of the striking-off in the official RCS compendium and loss of RCS standing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-owner (UBO) confirmation filing in the RBE register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des Beneficiaires Effectifs (RBE), Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On a rolling annual basis, within one month of the anniversary of the most recent RBE filing; additionally, within one month after any transfer of partnership interests or change in beneficial ownership, control rights, or applicable exemption
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or annually confirm UBO data is criminally sanctionable with a fine of EUR 500 to EUR 25,000 (approx. USD 550 to 27,500) per violation under the Law of 13 January 2019; the RBE registrar publishes non-compliant entities on an official list and the default blocks issuance of RCS extracts and administrative attestations.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The Luxembourg SCSp is not a legal person and is statutorily exempt from the mandatory appointment of a 'reviseur d'entreprises agree' and from the filing and publication of annual accounts, except where it qualifies as a 'grande entreprise' or 'entite d'interet public'; such qualification is tested by crossing at least two of the three thresholds under the revised Law of 19 December 2002 (balance-sheet total EUR 4.4 million; net turnover EUR 8.8 million; average workforce of 50). In all other cases, an audit is only required if imported by the partnership agreement or demanded by financing parties.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 using the official chart of accounts (Plan comptable normal); IFRS as adopted by the EU applies only where Luxembourg-law consolidation or listed-parent obligations exist. The SCSp must nonetheless maintain full commercial books and records under Articles 11 to 15 of the Luxembourg Code de commerce.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp files its UBO declaration electronically in the RBE using a LuxTrust certificate; the confirmation must be renewed annually within one month of the anniversary of the previous filing. Any transfer of partnership interests or variation in the percentage of economic rights, voting control, or the stated exemption category must be re-filed within one month of the date the SCSp obtains knowledge. The filing and the annual confirmation are free of charge.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800 to USD 4,200 per annum for a Luxembourg corporate-service provider supplying the registered office, domiciliation, registered agent, and RCS/RBE compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 per annum where the statutory audit exemption applies; approximately USD 9,000 to USD 30,000 per engagement if an agreed-upon audit or investor-required review is commissioned

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 15.00% national CIT headline rate on taxable income above EUR 175,000; effective 16.05% after 7% solidarity surcharge; combined headline rate with Luxembourg City municipal business tax at 6.75% is 24.94%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holidays in Luxembourg. A fiscally transparent SCSp is not subject to entity-level CIT; profits are taxed at partner level under their respective taxpayer status. Available preferential mechanisms for the underlying medical EMR/HealthTech activity include the Luxembourg IP Box regime (80% exemption on net qualifying IP income, yielding an effective combined rate of approximately 5.0% for qualified software IP), the participation exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains, and targeted R&D/investment credits.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited; no statutory terminal expiry. Carryback is not permitted. Loss utilisation remains subject to anti-abuse conditions on change of control and business continuity rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Luxembourg Corporate Income Tax Return (Formulaire 500 / CIT declaration series) filed through the ACD electronic filing portal via MyGuichet.lu with LuxTrust authentication. For a fiscally transparent SCSp, the SCSp itself files an annual partnership information return (accrual and allocation schedule), while each taxable partner reports the allocated profit share in its own corporate or individual income tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal year; no statutory quarterly CIT instalment returns unless quarterly prepayments are administratively imposed).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return for a fiscal year ending on 31 December is due by 31 December of the following calendar year; other balance sheet dates follow the same one-year interval. Extensions may be granted by the Luxembourg direct tax administration upon reasoned application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SCSp legal name, RCS registration number, registered office address, legal form code, Luxembourg tax identification number, and eCDF electronic filing identifier.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must ensure the SCSp return identifies each partner by name, tax residence, foreign taxpayer reference, and profit allocation percentage; a foreign address block must be completed for non-resident partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Confirmation that the SCSp is fiscally transparent; list of partners, tax residence of each partner, share of profits/losses, and any Luxembourg permanent establishment to which profit is attributable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should attach a valid certificate of tax residence and a statement of no Luxembourg permanent establishment if treaty protection or domestic transparency is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net commercial profit or loss per the statutory/annual accounts of the SCSp before allocation, including revenue from EMR SaaS subscriptions, software licence fees, implementation services, and related operating costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must reconcile the commercial result to Luxembourg taxable income only to the extent attributable to a Luxembourg PE or Luxembourg-source income; otherwise only the informational allocation is reported.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible expenses, tax-exempt income, depreciation differences, IP Box deductions, participation exemption claims, and any adjustments resulting from transfer pricing corrections.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should apply only Luxembourg-specific adjustments against Luxembourg-source profit; home-country tax adjustments are not recorded in the Luxembourg SCSp declaration.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allocation of taxable profit or tax loss to each partner in accordance with the SCSp partnership agreement and Luxembourg transparency rules, including the opening balance and use of any carryforward losses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should separately record their allocated share for credit purposes in their local jurisdiction; Luxembourg will not levy CIT on a transparent SCSp unless a partner carries on a Luxembourg trade through a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 - Withholding Tax and Cross-Border Payments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of any Luxembourg-source payments made by the SCSp that are subject to Luxembourg withholding tax, including potentially deemed dividends, interest, royalties, or licensing fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an SCSp, allocations to non-resident partners are generally not dividends and carry no Luxembourg withholding tax; if a payment is separately characterised as Luxembourg-source royalty income, the domestic 0% withholding rate and applicable treaty protocol must be declared.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative penalty of up to EUR 25,000 and a 10% surcharge on any assessed CIT, plus late-payment interest at 0.8% per month (9.6% per annum). Willful non-filing or false filing is punishable as tax fraud with criminal fines and imprisonment of responsible officers.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for distributions or allocations by a fiscally transparent SCSp, because the SCSp has no separate Luxembourg corporate taxpayer personality and allocations are not dividends. The ordinary Luxembourg domestic dividend withholding tax rate of 15% applies only when an actual Luxembourg tax-resident company distributes profits; such 15% may be reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive or an applicable double tax treaty.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke double tax treaty relief, the beneficial owner/partner must supply a valid certificate of tax residence issued by its home treaty jurisdiction to the Luxembourg withholding agent or paying entity before the payment date, together with a completed DTA relief questionnaire and, where required, a form 105 refund application. The Luxembourg taxpayer then files the relevant application with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration (ACD); paperwork must be held for audit and any refund claimed within the statutory limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic withholding tax is 0% on both cross-border interest and royalties. Consequently, outbound EMR software royalties and intercompany debt interest from an SCSp will not bear Luxembourg withholding tax. Under Luxembourg's double tax treaties, these rates are generally reduced to 0%; for royalties, certain treaties may provide for a 0%-5% residual source rate, but no Luxembourg domestic injection arises.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg imposes no statutory de minimis transaction threshold for transfer pricing documentation; all cross-border related-party transactions, including EMR software licence fees, development cost contributions, and management charges, must be substantiated on an arm's length basis. Mandatory CbCR, Master File, and Local File obligations attach when the ultimate group consolidated turnover equals or exceeds EUR 750,000,000. For smaller groups, contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is nevertheless expected whenever related-party transactions exceed approximately EUR 1,000,000 in aggregate or a tax adjustment risk exists.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not maintain a standalone Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) in the Gulf state sense. However, substantive economic presence is a condition of Luxembourg tax residence, treaty access, and the anti-avoidance rule under ATAD and the Luxembourg General Tax Law. An SCSp that qualifies as a mere letterbox vehicle, lacking local offices, active management, employees, bank accounts, and real decision-making functions in relation to the EMR software business, will be vulnerable to treaty benefit denial, re-characterisation as opaque, and challenge under the general anti-abuse rule.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully omitting taxable revenue derived from EMR SaaS subscriptions and software licensing, recording fictitious royalties to an offshore related shell, or concealing ultimate beneficial owners to prevent the Luxembourg revenue authority from attributing profit to the true economic owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud: imprisonment of up to 5 years and a fine of up to EUR 250,000, together with civil fraud penalties of 50%-100% of the evaded tax, late-payment interest at 0.8% per month, forfeiture of reliefs and treaty benefits, and publication of the tax assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SCSp general partner and any managing director who signed or caused a false return are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax and can face civil restitution, asset freezing orders, travel bans, director disqualification, and imprisonment upon criminal conviction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp as a tax conduit with no real Luxembourg substance: no office, no employees, no local management decisions, no active commercial activity, while the EMR software IP and clinical services contracts are managed from another jurisdiction solely to obtain treaty or partnership transparency benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of ATAD and Luxembourg GAAR to disregard the entity or arrangement; denial of treaty benefits; re-characterisation of the SCSp as a permanent establishment of the overseas parent; reassessment of profit plus interest and penalties of up to EUR 250,000; possible loss of Luxembourg corporate and partnership law favourable treatment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Because an SCSp is without legal personality, the general partner and managers are subject to unlimited commercial and tax liability; the corporate veil is not a shield. They may be pursued personally for taxes, restitution, and damages, and may face travel bans and imprisonment in the context of criminal tax or fraud proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to verify and file the ultimate beneficial owners of the SCSp in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), failure to maintain adequate anti-money laundering files for the medical EMR SaaS payments, or accepting subscription payments from sanctioned or high-risk counterparties without enhanced due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: RBE non-compliance carries administrative fines of up to EUR 250,000 plus daily default penalties; serious AML failures attract CSSF administrative fines up to EUR 1,250,000 or 10% of annual turnover, and criminal money-laundering sanctions include imprisonment up to 5 years and confiscation of assets.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal criminal exposure is direct rather than dependent on veil-piercing: officers who approve or omit required AML filings face personal fines, imprisonment, civil damages to affected patients or clients, travel bans, and disqualification from directorships.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Entering into non-arm's-length transactions between the SCSp and related technology affiliates, such as overpriced software development fees, inflated commission or royalty charges, zero-interest loans, or circular payments designed to strip taxable profit from Luxembourg without valid business substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg General Tax Law and OECD TP principles, the tax authorities reprice the transaction to an arm's length result, impose a primary adjustment, and require a secondary adjustment where applicable; late interest of 0.8% per month and penalties of 10%-50% of the under-declared tax are triggered, increasing to 100% in cases of deliberate misconduct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the SCSp general partner are personally liable for negligent or intentional transfer pricing documentation failures and resulting assessments; deliberate mispricing may expose them to criminal tax fraud charges, civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment.
